contract: See .github/agents/llama-parity.agent.md. Single request, GPU resident, F32 KV, context 1024, batch/chunk 512, fixed identical IDs and generation lengths. Two independent 3w/7m opposite-order rounds, >=1.05x each phase and no request latency regression against pinned llama.cpp. Fresh exact accepted Rust quality corpus plus runtime admission and Rust ABBA.

warp_screen.hypothesis: Assign one warp per row. Each lane computes the three original logical warp partials and folds them in the original tree; no activation staging or block barriers. Eight rows per CTA should improve scheduling enough to offset the extra per-lane work.
warp_screen.fixtures: Same four frozen decode-shaped Q4_K/Q6_K expert-down replays as v1.
warp_screen.gate: Bitwise and guarded; >=1.10x over the staged v1 median on every case before full-model testing. Keep v1 and v2 timing as separate arms.

next_screen.hypothesis: Width-768 expert down wastes five of eight packed-matvec warps per row. Pack two rows into one 256-thread CTA (three live warps per row) and stage their shared 768-element activation once. Preserve logical zero additions and the 128/64/32 and warp reduction tree.
next_screen.fixtures: Approved model, frozen layer-0 46-token capture and layer-37 32-token held-out capture; token positions 0 and last from each, captured expert IDs and ffn_down_inp, every down row, Q6_K and Q4_K.
next_screen.screen: Rotating CUDA events, three warmups and seven samples per arm; whole selected down launch including staging, production packed reduction control, guarded bitwise outputs and no unwritten values. Require >=1.10x median in all four cases before escalating to full-model gates.

hypothesis: Sharing the routing, activation components, and barriers in one CTA, then eliminating the intermediate up write/read and SwiGLU launch, offsets two independent accumulator sets without changing arithmetic.
screen: Rotating CUDA-event samples (3 warmups, 7 measured per arm), one event pair around both parallel grouping launches, quantize once, then separate gate/up and existing SwiGLU vs fused. Also time entire expert panel including down quantize and unchanged Q6_K down consuming the computed activation; independently verify frozen Q6_K down from its own frozen activation. Require frozen Q4_K/Q6_K baseline output hashes and exact candidate activation and downstream output bits and intact guards. Advance only at >=1.10x median replaced-path at both lengths and no >5% regression on either full expert panel. Existing quality/admission gates are unchanged.
note: The historical narrow binary, captures and current model pins verify; the historical archived source checksum predates the dirty worktree and was not restored. Compare newly built control against frozen output hashes.

owned_jobs.status: V1 ABBA timed out. V2 four-case ABBA, capacity and all three CUDA sanitizers completed.

decision: Exact MMA3 gate/up v1 rejected on held-out performance, despite exact outputs in all four replays. Development replaced-path speedups 1.171x/1.221x; held-out 1.137x (L37/T32) and 1.058x (L47/T46), below 1.10x. No production dispatch change or full-model admission.
decode_decision: V1 exact on replay and full quality, but rejected for default promotion: both completed decode arms miss 1.10x (timed 31-step decode about 1.088x/1.086x; complete decode request about 1.088x/1.086x). A2 timed out before 256/512 summaries; incomplete matrix must not be used for parity. V1 remains opt-in and not fully admitted.

quality.status: 990/990 bitwise snapshots, 30/30 independent generations, reset/error and exact-budget checks in the accepted MMA3 comparison; candidate reservation 18855091776 bytes
quality.reference_note: Fresh accepted MMA3 reference uses the archived quality harness in the same profile as the pinned accepted CLI. The initial F32-tiled run is a cross-arithmetic comparison and is not the bitwise admission reference.

warp_decision: All four replay arms exact. Warp design is 1.37x-1.50x faster than staged v1 and 1.82x-2.18x faster than packed control. V2 replaces v1 only under the opt-in feature; accepted binaries unchanged.

warp_candidate.quality: 990/990 bitwise snapshots and 30/30 independent generations, reset/error and exact-budget checks
warp_candidate.abba: 31-step decode 1.130x in both orders, complete decode request 1.130x in both orders, prefill and other measured phases within 5%, same reservation and public generated IDs. Rust vs Rust only; no default dispatch change.

warp_admission.capacity: Batch 31/32/46/128/255/512 with exact 1024 context and error/reset gates
warp_admission.sanitizers: memcheck 0 errors; racecheck 0 hazards; synccheck 0 errors on the new kernel

matched.boundary: Cold request state, reset included in total, synchronized prompt and each continuation step with device greedy selection on both engines. No model load or tokenization. Fixed continuation input IDs and separate free-greedy output.
matched.decision: No parity: Rust/llama.cpp speedups in both rounds were 0.206-0.208x / 0.237-0.239x / 0.175x at 46/256/512 prefill, and 0.675-0.676x at 31-step decode. Complete requests are slower in all four cases. Greedy IDs first differ at zero-based index 18 in the 32-output decode case only.

prefill_profile.decision: MMA3 was 79.0% of summed CUDA kernel time, attention 15.2%; prioritize MMA3. This profile covers two 512-token requests and is diagnostic only.

prefill_experiment.name: mma3-64-row-reuse
prefill_experiment.hypothesis: A 64-row by 32-assignment CTA amortizes activation staging and descriptor access over twice the output rows without raising per-thread accumulator count. Preserve the K32 order.
prefill_experiment.fixtures: Frozen L0/T46 and L0/T512 expert matrices; exact Q4_K/Q6_K with admitted grouping, common quantizer and captured-output bindings.
prefill_experiment.gate: Existing rotating replay, 3 warmups/7 samples per arm; require exact outputs and >=1.10x in all 512-token expert projections, no >5% regression at 46 tokens. Preparation is common, separately measured, and must be included in the decision.

prefill_decision: All six projections bitwise exact. Including common preparation, 512-token gate/up/down ratios 1.125x/1.131x/1.212x; 46-token ratios 0.972x/0.974x/1.015x. Development screen passed; candidate remains test-only.

prefill_heldout.decision: All six projections bitwise exact. Preparation-inclusive L37 ratios 1.130/1.127/1.166x; L47 ratios 1.132/1.135/1.211x. Advance only for 512-token grouped expert projections, against admitted warp decode research.

prefill_integration.decision: All 990 full-vocabulary digests and 30 independent generations match. Four-case ABBA against admitted warp decode: 512-token prefill and complete request 1.086x/1.084x in both orders, short/256/decode within 1%. Same memory and generated IDs. Misses 1.10x in both orders; do not promote or treat as admitted. Feature remains opt-in research.

attention_experiment.hypothesis: Two adjacent causal query positions in one CTA reuse each K and V read while independently preserving each original F32 score, softmax, and increasing-time value sum. Halving CTAs/query traffic offsets more registers and shared scores.
attention_experiment.fixtures: Capture Qcur/Kcur/Vcur and attn_attended on frozen 512-token development and held-out prompt IDs (cases-512.json) for layers 0 and 37. Screen all outputs, including causality and guards, against the admitted normalized/reused attention baseline.
attention_experiment.gate: 3 warmups/7 rotating CUDA-event samples around entire attention launch. Require bitwise outputs and >=1.10x median at development 512 before held-out 512; no promotion without the unchanged full-model gates.

attention_development.decision: All 2,097,152 outputs bitwise equal to capture and normalized/reused control. Median attention launch 0.5692 ms to 0.3036 ms (1.875x).

attention_heldout.decision: All 2,097,152 outputs exact; median 0.5664 ms to 0.3041 ms (1.863x). Test combined attention/wide-row package against admitted warp build; target >=1.10x in 512 prefill and complete request in both orders, with other phases no more than 5% slower.

attention_package.decision: Combined wide-row and query-pair package matches all 990 vocabulary snapshots and 30 independent generations, crosses package speed gates at 1.175x/1.173x for both 512-token prefill and complete request, other phases within 1%, no memory increase. Remains opt-in pending sanitizer and capacity checks.

attention_package_admission.capacity: Two 512-token chunks at exact 1024 context; all 151936 logits bitwise equal to prior admitted Rust build. Full quality also checked reset/error and numerical reservation.
attention_package_admission.sanitizers: Full request memcheck zero errors for the two kernels. Full-request racecheck exceeded the bounded job limit; representative first launch of each kernel on real-model operands checked separately with zero racecheck hazards and zero synccheck errors.

attention_package_matched.decision: No parity: Rust at 0.206-0.211x / 0.240x / 0.204-0.205x in 46/256/512 prefill, and 0.677x in 31-step decode; complete requests lag on all four. Separate free greedy diverges only on decode, first at index 18. Fixed timing paths remain identical inputs.

next_prefill_profile.decision: MMA3 accounts for 94.5% of 46-token kernel time and 83.6% at 512, with 30.3% at 512 still in the 32-row dense kernels.

dense_experiment.hypothesis: Dense projections have fully occupied token tiles (except a tail) and can amortize activation staging across 64 output rows; test whether the distinct dense shape benefits without reordering arithmetic.
dense_experiment.fixtures: Frozen development layer-0 46/256/512 Q/K/V/O tensors, all output bits and guards; held-out 256/512 layers 37/47 only after development.
dense_experiment.gate: Use 3 warmups/7 alternating samples plus common quantizer (Q/K/V charge divided by 3) and >=1.10x in each targeted case. No dispatch change on a development-only result.

dense_development.decision: All 12 projections bitwise exact. All 512-token projections pass >=1.10x including preparation (Q/K/V/O 1.298/1.116/1.136/1.174x); do not change 46 or 256 dispatch.

dense_heldout.decision: All eight projections exact, 1.116x-1.297x preparation-inclusive; advance scoped dense-only extension at 512. Test against the admitted combined package (not the older warp-only binary).

dense_package.decision: Full quality exact (990/990 and 30/30), but incremental 512-token Rust ABBA 1.047x/1.046x for prefill and complete request, below 1.10x in both orders. Do not promote or use as admitted baseline.

compact_expert_experiment.hypothesis: Emit native 8-assignment descriptors from the existing parallel expert counts, then launch one 64-thread MMA3 kernel per projection. Unlike the failed two-pass narrow mapping, use one launch and a compact 9-word stride; split larger expert counts into several independent descriptors without changing K accumulation.
compact_expert_experiment.fixtures: Frozen L0/T46 development; held-out L47/T46 only after success. Both use captured gate/up/down operands and GPU descriptors independently bound to CPU.
compact_expert_experiment.gate: Require bitwise equality with frozen MMA3 outputs and intact guards. Alternating CUDA events (3 warmups/7 samples) for complete expert panel including count, emission, quantization, separate gate/up, SwiGLU, and down; advance only at >=1.10x including all preparation.

compact_expert_development.initial_failure: CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND for group_parallel_emit32; moved both entry points out of the helper to file scope and rebuilt.
compact_expert_development.result: Exact L0/T46 replay; 0.813952 ms control vs 0.626528 ms compact (1.299x), including both grouping launches and the complete expert panel.

compact_expert_heldout.result: Exact L47/T46 replay; 0.541344 ms control vs 0.538080 ms compact (1.006x). Rejected below 1.10x complete-panel gate; test-only.

warp_register_experiment.hypothesis: Keep 32-row/32-token geometry and per-group floating-point order but have each warp load its INT8 MMA fragments and metadata into registers directly. Eliminating shared-memory staging and both CTA barriers per K group may outweigh duplicate global loads in short dense projections. Distinct from previous shared asynchronous pipelines and narrow expert mappings.
warp_register_experiment.fixtures: All four dense Q/K/V/O projections at frozen development L0/T46; if all pass, unchanged at frozen held-out L47/T46.
warp_register_experiment.gate: Bitwise equal to captured MMA3 and intact guards. For each of four projections, require at least 1.10x median CUDA-event speedup including common quantization (3 warmups/7 alternating samples). No runtime integration before held-out success.

warp_register_development.result: All four L0/T46 output digests match frozen MMA3, with intact guards. Including preparation, Q/K/V/O reached 0.809x/0.797x/1.167x/0.793x respectively. Rejected because three Q4_K projections were slower; no held-out run or dispatch.

q4_planar_experiment.hypothesis: Transpose packed Q4_K words within each 32-row tile into K-block/word/row order, preserving exactly 144 bytes per block and decoded values. Hold activation staging, geometry and accumulation fixed to isolate weight load coalescing; no permanent second device copy in a future integration.
q4_planar_experiment.fixtures: Frozen L0/T46 Q/K/O development, with held-out L47/T46 Q4_K dense shapes if development passes. Verify exact replay against frozen MMA3 digests.
q4_planar_experiment.gate: Intact guards and bitwise exact; at least 1.10x for each eligible development projection including common quantization (3 warmups/7 alternating samples). Host layout conversion excluded from steady-state screen; record its cost separately. No production dispatch before held-out and full quality.

q4_planar_development.result: All three L0/T46 Q4_K digests match frozen MMA3 and guards pass. Including preparation, Q/K/O reached 1.061x/1.059x/1.050x. Host conversion took 1.200/0.123/0.973 ms respectively and preserved byte counts. Rejected below 1.10x; no held-out run or dispatch.

short_decode_profile.result: Explicit CUDA graph-node trace on the admitted fixed-ID comparator. Packed matvec takes 56.4% of traced kernel time; gate/up form its largest shape bucket (66.67 ms across 6144 launches, 24.7% of all traced kernel time). Normalize takes 11.0%, warp down 9.5%. Default graph granularity did not expose kernel records.

packed_decode_gate_up_experiment.hypothesis: For decode only, one CTA per selected expert and output row computes packed gate and up from the same input with the existing packed lane dot products and independent 256-thread reduction trees, then writes SwiGLU. This removes two graph nodes without the shared matrix tiles of rejected prefill fusion.
packed_decode_gate_up_experiment.fixtures: Frozen L0/T46 position 0 and 45 ffn_norm plus routed IDs; held-out L47/T46 positions 0 and 45 only after both development positions pass.
packed_decode_gate_up_experiment.gate: Bitwise identical activation, intact guards, finite outputs and >=1.10x for complete gate/up/SwiGLU at both positions, with 3 warmups/7 alternating samples. Full quality and Rust ABBA required before integration.

packed_decode_gate_up_development.result: Both positions exact with intact guards; full gate/up/SwiGLU medians 23.840 vs 16.320 us (1.461x) and 22.784 vs 16.864 us (1.351x).

packed_decode_gate_up_heldout.result: Both positions exact with guards; medians 23.616 vs 16.384 us (1.441x) and 23.712 vs 16.736 us (1.417x). Passed replay only.

packed_decode_gate_up_quality.result: Opt-in package passed 990/990 full-vocabulary digests and 30/30 free-greedy ID vectors against the accepted MMA3 reference. No performance admission yet.

packed_decode_gate_up_abba.result: Both orders improved decode and complete request by 1.087x/1.085x, below 1.10x. All four greedy ID checks match and prefill is unchanged within measurement variation. Not admitted; remains opt-in. Admitted comparator unchanged.

decode_normalize_experiment.hypothesis: The admitted normalize already uses the exact warp-tail reduction, so do not retest it. For width 2048, retain eight input values per CTA lane and compute the final inverse only once in the reducing warp, then broadcast the inverse instead of the sum. Preserve the existing per-lane F32 chain and reduction tree.
decode_normalize_experiment.fixtures: Frozen ffn_inp, actual GGUF normalization weights and ffn_norm reference at L0/T46 positions 0 and 45, followed by held-out L47/T46 if both pass.
decode_normalize_experiment.gate: Bitwise against admitted normalize, intact guards and at least 1.10x in the complete normalize launch at both positions, with 3 warmups/7 alternating samples. No production dispatch until held-out success.

decode_normalize_development.result: Both positions bitwise equal to the admitted path and captured outputs, with intact guards. Median speedups 1.401x and 1.375x.

decode_normalize_heldout.result: Both positions bitwise equal to admitted normalize and captured outputs. Position 0 reached 1.154x, but position 45 reached 1.048x, below 1.10x. Rejected; not combined with gate/up.

dense_decode_k_pair_experiment.hypothesis: One physical lane performs two logical 256-thread K tasks that are combined at the first 128-stride of the admitted reduction. Halving the CTA size without changing the tree may improve useful residency for dense decode; this is not the previous width-768 expert down warp mapping.
dense_decode_k_pair_experiment.fixtures: Frozen L0/T46 Q and O inputs at positions 0 and 45; advance only to unchanged held-out L47/T46 if all four pass.
dense_decode_k_pair_experiment.gate: Bitwise against admitted packed decode and intact guards. At least 1.10x on each complete single matvec launch, 3 warmups/7 alternating samples.

dense_decode_k_pair_development.result: All four outputs bitwise exact with intact guards, but Q positions 0/45 reached 0.977x/1.043x and O reached 1.007x/0.950x. Rejected; no held-out or production dispatch.

synchronous_k64_experiment.hypothesis: Stage two K32 groups before a single CTA barrier pair, then consume them in increasing K order. For Q4_K, reuse the loaded packed byte word for both nibbles. No asynchronous copy or overlapping pipeline; descriptors, quantization and floating-point reduction order unchanged.
synchronous_k64_experiment.fixtures: Complete L0/T46 frozen expert panel; advance only after success to held-out L47/T46. Replace Q4_K gate/up only, keep Q6_K down.
synchronous_k64_experiment.gate: Check all three frozen projection digests, guarded end-to-end activation and down outputs, and independent descriptor binding. Require at least 1.10x in the whole panel (including preparation) with 3 warmups/7 alternating samples.

synchronous_k64_development.result: Exact L0/T46 frozen bindings, end-to-end activation/down and intact guards. Whole-panel median 0.812384 vs 0.646624 ms (1.256x). Initial NVRTC run exposed a missing prototype guard on the reduction helper; widened the guard and rebuilt before measurement.

synchronous_k64_heldout.result: Exact L47/T46 outputs and intact guards. Whole-panel median 0.541664 vs 0.522688 ms (1.036x), below 1.10x. Rejected; no dispatch.

short_prefill_routing_analysis.result: Both fixtures carry 368 assignments. L0 uses 85 live 32-column descriptors and 98 compact8 descriptors (+15%); L47 uses 54 and 77 (+43%). Tile32 padding is 2352 vs 1360 columns, respectively. Compact8's extra tiles are more pronounced on held-out routing; the counts alone do not prove the timing cause.

mixed_expert_tile_experiment.hypothesis: Keep existing 32-assignment descriptors and the full 32-column shape for descriptors containing more than 8 assignments. Pair two short descriptors per 128-thread CTA, with independent 64-thread shared tiles and synchronization, so work for medium experts is not split. CPU fixture analysis predicts 85 to 49 live CTA descriptors per row tile on L0 and 54 to 37 on L47, before accounting for preparation overhead or occupancy.
mixed_expert_tile_experiment.fixtures: Complete L0/T46 frozen expert panel followed by L47/T46 unchanged if development passes.
mixed_expert_tile_experiment.gate: Check schedule against CPU, all captured projection and activation/down bits against MMA3, and guards. At least 1.10x median in the entire expert panel including schedule, grouping and quantization (3 warmups/7 alternating samples).

mixed_expert_tile_progress.result: Test-only warp-ballot emitter compiled by NVRTC and matched the independent CPU schedule and guards for L0 and L47 (49 and 37 live CTA descriptors). No subgroup MMA3 mapping or performance result exists yet.

mixed_expert_tile_development.result: The subgroup MMA3 mapping passed bitwise frozen gate/up/down, complete activation/down and guard checks. L0/T46 complete median was 0.814688 ms baseline vs 2.191680 ms mixed (0.372x). Rejected; no held-out performance or production dispatch. Reduced live CTA count did not translate into speed; no stall or register-spill attribution was measured.

mixed_expert_resource_diagnosis.result: Driver predicts only 1 resident 128-thread CTA per SM for mixed vs 8 for baseline. Both use 64 registers/thread and zero local bytes; static shared allocation is 11776 vs 5888 bytes. Compact8 predicts 20 resident 64-thread CTAs. The occupancy constraint is real in the driver model; exact stall and barrier allocation causes were not measured.

mixed_uniform_development.result: Uniform CTA barriers and one shared union recovered 8 predicted blocks/SM (64 registers, 5888 shared bytes, zero local bytes). L0/T46 was bitwise exact; complete panel 0.815040 vs 0.633344 ms (1.287x).

mixed_uniform_heldout.result: Bitwise exact panel and intact guards. Held-out L47/T46 whole-panel median 0.542336 vs 0.527936 ms (1.027x), below 1.10x. Rejected; no dispatch or comparator promotion.

medium_prefill_profile.result: At 256 tokens MMA3 consumes 87.3% of traced kernel time. Grouped gate/up and down together used 124.78 ms across two traced requests, versus 62.75 ms for remaining MMA3 projections. Frozen L0/L37/L47 have 107/122/108 live tile32 descriptors and 1376/1856/1408 padded columns from 2048 assignments each.

medium_wide_expert_experiment.hypothesis: The 64-row grouped tile admitted only at 512 tokens may also amortize activation staging at 256 tokens. This does not retry the short-panel column designs; this shape is currently on the 32-row path.
medium_wide_expert_experiment.fixtures: Existing frozen 256-token L0 expert projections for the first screen; L37 and L47 only if L0 passes.
medium_wide_expert_experiment.gate: Require bitwise equality to 32-row replay outputs, intact guards, and at least 1.10x in the median three-projection panel including count/emission and both quantizations, using 3 warmups/7 alternating samples. Report per-projection medians as diagnostics.

medium_wide_expert_estimate.result: L0/T256 gate/up/down matched the 32-row outputs bitwise and improved 1.122x/1.129x/1.239x individually. Summing medians with common preparation gives 1.303072 vs 1.137024 ms (1.146x); this is a screening estimate, not directly timed full-panel evidence.

medium_wide_expert_development.result: Direct L0/T256 panel matched all frozen projection digests plus activation and downstream output with guards. Median 1.234336 vs 1.072544 ms (1.151x), including grouping, two quantizations and SwiGLU.

medium_wide_expert_heldout.result: Both panels were bitwise exact. L37 reached 1.087x (1.350560 vs 1.242592 ms), below the 1.10x gate, while L47 reached 1.152x (1.265184 vs 1.098048 ms). No 256-token dispatch change; the admitted 512-token scope is unchanged.

medium_same_expert_weight_reuse.hypothesis: Pair adjacent tile32 descriptors only when both belong to the same expert. Use one 32-row weight staging tile for both assignment tiles while keeping separate activation tiles and independent ordered accumulators. Leave singleton descriptors on the existing path. Frozen L0/L37/L47 contain 20/21/20 eligible pairs out of 107/122/108 live descriptors; the possible weight reload reduction is 17.2-18.7%, not a measured speedup.
medium_same_expert_weight_reuse.fixtures: Complete L0/T256 panel first, then L37/T256 and L47/T256 only on success.
medium_same_expert_weight_reuse.gate: Check the schedule against CPU, all frozen projection and activation/down digests, and guards. Require at least 1.10x in the whole panel including grouping, scheduling and quantization with 3 warmups/7 alternating samples.
medium_same_expert_weight_reuse.gpu: No compute processes at the post-run check.

medium_same_expert_schedule.result: Test-only GPU schedule exactly matched the CPU oracle and intact guards on frozen L0/T256: 20 pairs, 87 live entries instead of 107. No shared-weight MMA3 kernel or timing result yet. No GPU compute processes at the post-run check.

medium_same_expert_development.result: Shared-weight tile64 matched frozen projections, activation and downstream output with guards, but the complete L0/T256 panel regressed from 1.236672 ms to 1.582016 ms (0.782x). Rejected; no held-out timing or dispatch.

medium_same_expert_resources.result: Compared with baseline, the shared-weight kernel increased from 64 to 102 registers/thread and from 5888 to 10240 shared bytes, with zero local bytes on both. Predicted active 128-thread CTAs fell from 8 to 4 per SM. The result establishes a resource trade-off, not measured stall causality.

medium_same_expert_warp8.hypothesis: An eight-warp (256-thread) same-expert mapping splits paired 64-column descriptors across warps (16x16 per warp, preserving 24 accumulators/lane) and splits 32-column singletons across all eight warps (16x8 per warp), recovering SM warp residency while sharing one 32-row weight tile per same-expert pair.

resources.result: Single-body residual_matmul_mma3_same_expert_warp8 uses 56 registers/thread, 10496 shared bytes, 0 local bytes, and 4 predicted 256-thread CTAs/SM (1024 active threads/SM, matching baseline 8x128 and rows64 4x256, vs 512 active threads/SM on the 102-reg 128-thread mapping).

development.result: Bitwise exact against frozen L0/T256 gate/up/down digests, SwiGLU activation, downstream output, quantizer and schedule guards. Improved over the 128-thread mapping (1.582016 ms -> 1.325536 ms), but complete L0/T256 panel still regressed against baseline (1.232768 ms baseline vs 1.325536 ms candidate, 0.930x; replaced path 0.806912 ms vs 0.914208 ms, 0.883x), below the 1.10x gate. Rejected; no held-out run or dispatch.

dense_splitk_experiment.hypothesis: Dense prefill MMA3 launches with <=512 base CTAs underutilize the RTX 5090's 170 SMs and expose the ~100-200 us single-CTA serial K loop. Splitting K across power-of-two slices (k_slice >= 128, up to 1024 CTAs) into existing workspace scratch (<=4 MiB, L2-resident) with a deterministic increasing-slice coalesced reduction fills a single GPU wave without adding reservation.

resources.result: residual_matmul_mma3_splitk uses 66 registers/thread, 5888 shared bytes, 0 local bytes, and 7 predicted 128-thread CTAs/SM (1190 concurrent CTAs across 170 SMs).

development.result: All 9 targeted (splits >= 2) L0 projections passed >=1.10x preparation-inclusive with intact partial/output guards: T46 Q/K/V/O 2.088x/6.384x/7.097x/3.620x (complete panel 3.730x); T256 K/V/O 2.933x/2.802x/1.199x (complete panel 1.358x); T512 K/V 2.011x/1.834x (complete panel 1.120x). Untargeted splits=1 projections remained bitwise exact; worst max_abs vs F32 dropped or matched (<=4.17e-7).

heldout.result: Frozen binary passed all 18 targeted held-out projections across L37 and L47 at T46/T256/T512: T46 panels 3.768x (L37) and 3.721x (L47); T256 panels 1.358x (L37) and 1.358x (L47); T512 panels 1.129x (L37) and 1.122x (L47). Worst max_abs 1.22e-4, min cosine 0.999999999999749.

attention_even_extension.result: Extending bitwise-preserving attention_fused_query_pair to even lengths >=32 matched all captured outputs bitwise with intact guards: L0 T46 1.332x, L0 T256 1.854x; held-out L37 T46 1.332x, L37 T256 1.840x.

splitk_package.quality: Passed all 990 full-vocabulary snapshots and 30 independent generations against both fresh f32-tiled (max_abs 0.0007615 <= 0.01, min_cosine 0.99999999964 >= 0.99999, 0 argmax/gen mismatches, 132/132 short fallback snapshots bitwise) and fresh accepted-mma3 (max_abs 0.0009174, min_cosine 0.99999999936, 0 argmax/gen mismatches). Reservation unchanged at 18855091776 bytes.
splitk_package.abba: Against admitted pair-package (ce4ca2d4...): 46-token prefill 1.425x/1.425x and complete short request 1.250x/1.249x in both orders (>=1.10x package gate passed); 256-token prefill 1.141x/1.140x (request 1.099x/1.097x); 512-token prefill and request 1.072x/1.070x; 31-step decode 1.001x/1.000x. Identical generated IDs and reservation.

admission.capacity: Batch 31/32/46/128/255 and exact 1024 context all passed quality, reservation, one-over and poison/reset gates; batch 31 remained 100% bitwise exact.
admission.sanitizers: Scoped batch-32 real-model memcheck (18 launches: 0 errors), racecheck (9 launches: 0 hazards), synccheck (9 launches: 0 errors); strict Clippy and fmt clean.

splitk_package.decision: Admitted as new opt-in research comparator (target/llama-parity-splitk/release/local-inference). Default dispatch and accepted binary unchanged.

decode_fusion_experiment.hypothesis: Single-token decode launches separate Q/K/V packed matvecs (3 graph nodes), separate Q/K head_norm, rotary and cache_kv (5 graph nodes), and a 256-thread 80-barrier router. Fusing Q/K/V packed matvecs, fusing 128-dim head_norm+RoPE+KV-cache, and replacing 128-expert top-8 routing with a barrier-free 1-warp register shuffle preserve exact IEEE-754 bits and combine with held-out-validated packed-decode-gate-up.

development.result: On frozen L0/T46 positions 0 and 45, all four components were bitwise exact with intact guards: matvec_packed_qkv 1.457x/1.484x, qkv_head_norm_rope_cache 1.879x/1.843x, router_warp128 1.882x/1.812x; residual_normalize reached 0.861x/1.385x and was rejected (<1.10x at pos 0).

heldout.result: Frozen binary on held-out L47/T46 positions 0 and 45 passed all three surviving components bitwise with guards: matvec_packed_qkv 1.406x/1.472x, qkv_head_norm_rope_cache 1.972x/2.928x, router_warp128 1.849x/1.860x.

Free-greedy IDs match exactly on short/prefill/long and first differ at zero-based index 18 on 32-step decode, unchanged from accepted MMA3.
